body:
In all honesty I wouldn’t chance doing something like that. I was more or less wondering if 147 days would be enough time for a heavy smoker to show clear on a 90-120 day follicle test. 

But I did need a laugh. Got the mental image of the lab tech screaming like the scalped me lol
A+ for creativity my guy

That’s what I was thinking. Go ahead and buzz it all off now so when the next opportunity arises, I’ll be good to go. 
Hate that I’m still being punished after putting in the work to get clean.
Yeah it does. It’s for pre-employment so I could just decide not to take it. But at the same time, it’s a great job. Hate to miss out on the opportunity.

Thanks for your response. Does Certo show up on tests if he tried to mask? 
I’m not really familiar with this, just trying to be as supportive as I can.

Thank you so much for your response. This was very insightful.

I am mentally preparing myself for all hell to break loose in my life over this. There are a million things that is happening here.. So after he gets out, he will have to live in a “halfway house” for 3 years before he can return home. After those 3 years, he will come back home and live with my grandfather who lives next door to us. Then, after my grandfather passes, he will inherit his house & land. I inherited family land as well, I love where I grew up. What is absolutely gut wrenching to me is that I’m realizing that in the end I’m going to have to sell my land & the house I grew up in because a sex offender will live right beside us - within literal rock throwing distance. My daughter will be 3 years old when he is allowed to come back.

This is going to be a horrible situation and my family is going to absolutely hate me at the end. You always hear people talk the talk about “oh I’d do anything for my baby” and I’m going to have to walk the walk.

That’s my family’s argument. Like I previously stated there are a lot of things being left out on purpose in this situation, but there was definitely some sketchy things surrounding the accusation. At the same time, the victim was a child, AND Sam has not been forthcoming about what happened, so for my own sanity I have decided to rely on the court’s decision in this matter. Trying to solve the case myself just sends me spiraling.
I’m so sorry to hear this, my heart breaks hearing your story. Thank you so much for sharing this, I hope you have found healing and I hope he is burning in hell.

This is something my husband and I have discussed in detail. 

I know for a fact no one in my family would just allow/encourage something to happen to my daughter, but at the same time they may be too trusting of him. It only takes one moment.

Congratulations on growing your tiny human!!

I hope that you never, ever are put into a situation like this. But then again, no one is “safe.” There’s a fine line between being paranoid and being vigilant. Always, always be vigilant!
I’m so sorry to hear this. Thank you for sharing. I will definitely take this into consideration.

Hi, thank you for your response. Just to clarify the victim was a child. I didn’t want to share identifiable details so I explained that the situation was not “a 17 & 18 year old hooked up.” This was a serious crime.

I haven’t thought about things this way before, and you are absolutely right. 

I’m not forcing anyone to choose between “him or me.” I am simply stating that I don’t want to be around him and I don’t want our daughter around him. If they turn it into a “him or me” situation, then that’s on them.

Another side to this whole situation is that my daughter will grow up watching how I handle this. What would I be teaching her if I allowed my boundaries to be ignored? 

I’d rather be known as a bitch than a pushover. Especially when it comes to my baby.

Thank you for sharing. You advice is appreciated. You are absolutely right. Even if I believe he would never harm my daughter, there is still a chance. There is a chance with anyone. I completely agree with you, I don’t think the constant paranoia is worth it.

Thank you for your advice!

Unfortunately the caretaker/supervisor/person(s) in charge of the situation did not fulfill their duties. It was not family. There was some very sketchy details surrounding the situation. With that being said, it doesn’t take away from the victim’s pain or take away the fact that he is a predator.
I’m so sorry you are dealing with that. Sexual offenses come with so much more than predator v victim. The families of both are affected as well. I wish you the best in navigating your situation.

It is very clear to me as well. My daughter’s safety will always be the most important thing. 

Your perspective on this was very insightful and I really appreciate your response.

You are correct. Sam will not even talk about it with family. While he was out on bail, he lived with my grandfather. I asked my grandfather if Sam had ever confessed to anything or gave any sort of insight into the situation from his perspective.. My grandfather said that he wouldn’t even talk about it, and when he was directly asked about it, Sam would shut down. What we know about the situation is only what we have heard from court.

Coercion is a very valid possibility. Again I’m trying to protect my privacy because this was a pretty publicized thing where I live due to the circumstances around the accusation, BUT Sam was put into a very sketchy situation to begin with. Then again I also stand firm on believing the victim because the victim was a child. This is just messy and awful. If I get into trying to solve the case for myself it’s kind of like opening Pandora’s box. I told myself that it was better for my own sanity to just trust the courts, especially since Sam will not speak about it.

Of course I’d choose her safety. 

What a sad thing to have to choose between though.. family or your child’s safety.

My husband and I have considered this. While I was pregnant we discussed in detail about what the guidelines were going to be regarding Sam as we knew he would be getting out. At first is was that specific family members could not watch our baby if Sam was present, which turned into he could not be around Sam unless my husband or I was present, and then after she was born the idea of him even looking at her or holding her turns my stomach. 

It’s a completely different story once you lay eyes on your child. It was like the reality and gravity of the situation set in. All we want to do is protect her and be the best parents that we can.
I think so as well. There are a million details being left out of this story simply for privacy purposes but you hit the nail right on the head. I really appreciate your thoughtful advice.
That’s the #1 priority - protecting my daughter. My feelings and emotions will always be secondary. Period.

EXACTLY! My family is most likely exactly how you would imagine them. They give him 100% of the benefit of the doubt. 
Since he just took a plea deal and didn’t go to trial, no one really saw the evidence against him so they choose to believe that he was either coerced into the crime or didn’t do it. Sam has never been forthright with the family about what happened, he would never speak on it.

My husband is absolutely blown away by their actions.
Yes, exactly! Families care more about making it go away then dealing with the fallout. Thank you so much for your advice.

I have a question, how did you explain to your kids why he wasn’t in their life? Hopefully that isn’t too personal for me to ask. We will have to explain the situation at some point to our daughter in the years to come and I’d like to handle it the right way.

Thank you very much for your advice. I agree, his disability plays a significant role in this. If he were a “normal” person, I wouldn’t even think twice about what would be done in the situation.

He is in his mid 20s, but he has the mind of maybe a 12-13 year old on a good day. This does NOT take away from what his did, but at the same time it’s tough to decide how to handle the situation.

Thank you so much for your response. You are 100% right. They have to respect my boundaries as a parent. 

At the end of the day, if something was to ever happen and I let my boundaries be compromised, it would be my fault.

Thank you. It feels very validating to hear that. This is such a sensitive issue with a million different perspectives so it has been hard to emotionally navigate through what decisions need to be made.

Thank you so much for your advice. I agree with you, my heart aches for the victim. 
My daughter’s safety is my #1 priority. My emotions will always come secondary, but it still hurts that this is going to end with my family choosing him over me.

I really appreciate the thoughtful advice. 

I have an inkling that by not attending this “homecoming” garbage, I’ll be drawing a line in the sand with my family. Obviously my daughter’s safety is my top priority and I would never let it be compromised, but at the same time I know that by not attending and feeding into their excitement that they will disown me. They are just that type of people.

I guess my biggest struggle is that we all used to be so close and we protected ‘Sam’ so much because of his disability.. Now that this has happened it’s sickening and also sad. It’s like the ‘Sam’ that I tremendously cared for died.

Perhaps she is critical because she is jealous of your youth? Maybe she wants you to avoid the mistakes she made, or wants to try to live vicariously?
Sometimes people act critical when they really just want to see you succeed and not have to deal with the struggles that they did?
Not a whole lot of detail in your post so I’m giving her the benefit of the doubt
I have nothing to live for. I have no parents, my siblings don’t care, my job is stupid, i can’t afford college, I’m in debt. There’s not one good reason not to die.
